prerequisites: Prior knowledge in fluid mechanics, electricity, mechanisms, construction, and business management is recommended.
Spanish and English language skills (reading level for English).
Skills in using a calculator, creating and handling graphics, and technical drawing.

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.
Students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.

Students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on incomplete or limited information, including reflections on social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
Students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.
The ability to solve problems in new or little-known environments within multidisciplinary contexts related to energy engineering.
The ability to integrate knowledge to formulate applications for the development of new energy technologies.

The ability for autonomous learning that allows continued study through the development of the capacity to search for specialized documentation in cutting-edge scientific-technical literature and its assimilation.
Capacity for identification, analysis, and evaluation of the basic dominant phenomena in fluid-mechanical processes and energy transfer and utilization in engineering and industry.
Fundamental analysis of fluid-mechanical and thermal problems of interest in the energy industry, identifying strong and weak variables and evaluating possible simplifying hypotheses.
Performance of elementary calculations for sizing, selection of machines and equipment, and operation for installations with fluids with energy transfers.

Capacity for the study and proposal and application of different types of technologies to improve the utilization and energy efficiency of installations or plants, comparing alternatives by performance and costs.
Knowledge of the advances and latest trends regarding general equipment and operating characteristics of hydraulic and wind power plants.
Identify the different components of horizontal and vertical axis wind turbines.
Calculate and select the optimal aerodynamic profile for a wind turbine with specific performance.
Design a wind turbine for maximum utilization of wind characteristics in a given location.

syllabus_topics: Wind turbine technology: types of turbines and basic components.
Aerodynamics of wind turbines: actuator disk theory, dimensionless parameters, typical aerodynamic profiles, design optimization methods, and power control in wind turbines.
Loads on wind turbines: stationary, transient, cyclic, and random loads in wind turbines.
Horizontal axis wind turbines: rotors, power transmission systems, blade change mechanisms, and orientation mechanisms.
Vertical axis turbines: rotors, power transmission systems, and self-starting.

assessment_methods.method: Activities in laboratory practicals and power plant visits (results sheet delivery)
Activities in classroom practicals (results sheet delivery)

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, the final grade is 40% from the final exam and 60% from practical activities. To pass, a non-null score must be obtained in each block of the exam, and a minimum of 4 out of 10 points must be achieved on the exam. In extraordinary calls, the exam constitutes 100% of the final grade. Notes from practical classes are valid only for the ordinary call of the current academic year.
